userStories.title: nax-agent: MCP read-only hints, discovered providers and guarded asks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept discovered session providers and ask before non-read-only discovered tool execution in ask-profile sessions.

**Motivation** — The session API refuses MCP providers.

**Approach** — **1. nax-agent: read-only hints, discovered providers, guarded asks (US-001).**

- `McpToolInfo` (`packages/nax-agent/src/mcp/types.ts`) gains `readonly readOnly?: true`.
  `toolInfo(raw)` in `src/mcp/connect.ts` sets `readOnly: true` exactly when
  `raw.annotations` is an object whose `readOnlyHint` is the boolean `true`; in every other
  case the property is absent (not `undefined`), so a tool with no annotations keeps today's
  exact shape.
- `ProviderTool` (`src/tools/provider-types.ts`) gains `readonly readOnly?: boolean`.
  `sanitizeProviderTools` already spreads the tool, so the hint survives sanitisation.
- `ResolvedProviderTools` (`src/tools/provider-advertise.ts`) gains
  `readonly askTools?: readonly string[]`: the advertised (namespaced) names of tools that
  came from a `discovered` provider and whose `readOnly` is not `true`, in advertise order.
  Absent when the list would be empty. A `static` provider's tools never appear in it: their
  schemas are authored in this repo, and the skills tool must not ask on every load.
- `NativeBackendOptions.toolProviders` accepts `kind: "discovered"` as well as `"static"`;
  the zod check becomes `provider.kind === "static" || provider.kind === "discovered"`, and
  its message becomes `must be an array of tool providers with id, kind, stages and tools()`.
  Sanitisation of discovered tools already happens inside `resolveProviderTools` by kind.
- `buildSessionToolSupport` (`src/session/session-tool-support.ts`): when `args.profile` is
  `"ask"`, the ask rules passed to `buildCodingToolSupport` are `askRulesFor(...)` followed by
  one `{ tool: name, patterns: ["*"] }` per name in `args.providerTools?.askTools`. Every
  other profile adds none, so `full` (chat full mode) never asks for an MCP tool.
- The ask that results is an ordinary `approval_requested` event whose `tool` is the
  namespaced name. `approvalMemoryKey` already returns the tool name for a non-execute tool,
  so the chat's "allow for this session" remembers an MCP tool by name with no change.

**Scope** — In: shared MCP metadata, provider advertisement, native option validation and session ask rules; update the existing native-backend-providers AC-10 to accept discovered providers while AC-11 keeps rejecting malformed options with AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS. Out: nax transport/config mapping (US-002), chat composition (US-007), and lock format changes. A server's `readOnlyHint` is trusted as the server states it and is not pinned by the lock; the lock pins input schemas only, so a server that flips the hint after locking changes whether guarded mode asks.

**Interface** — Add `readonly readOnly?: true` to `McpToolInfo`, `readonly readOnly?: boolean` to `ProviderTool`, and `readonly askTools?: readonly string[]` to `ResolvedProviderTools`; keep `nativeBackend({ model, toolProviders: [provider] })`, `resolveProviderTools(providers, stage, workdir, options?)` and `buildSessionToolSupport(args)` as the existing entry points. Tests use coding-tool interactions and the normal ask port, not a special MCP approval path.

[unit] In that ask-profile session, a coding-tool interaction for acme__get emits no approval_requested event.
[unit] Opening with profile full and the discovered provider acme, a coding-tool interaction for acme__put emits no approval_requested event.

userStories.title: nax MCP layer: HTTP transport and read-only metadata
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend nax MCP configuration and connections to HTTP and carry shared read-only metadata into discovered provider tools.

**Motivation** — One MCP client, not two.

**Approach** — **2. HTTP transport and the read-only hint in nax's MCP layer (US-002).**

- `McpToolDescriptor` (`packages/nax/src/mcp/types.ts`) gains `readonly readOnly?: true`.
  `connectMcpServer` already returns the shared layer's tool objects unchanged, so the hint
  set by US-001 arrives with no mapping. `createMcpProviders` (`src/mcp/provider.ts`) maps
  each admitted tool to a `ProviderTool` that carries `readOnly: true` when the descriptor
  has it and no `readOnly` key otherwise. Without this mapping every MCP tool would land in
  `askTools`.
- `McpServerSchema` (`packages/nax/src/config/schemas-mcp.ts`): `command` becomes optional;
  new `url: z.string().url().optional()` and `headers: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).default({})`.
  The object keeps `.strict()` and gains a refinement: exactly one of `command` and `url` is
  set, with the message `set exactly one of command or url`.
- `McpServerConfig` (`src/config/runtime-types-mcp.ts`): `command?: string`, `url?: string`,
  `headers?: Record<string, string>` (optional in the interface so existing typed literals
  still compile; the schema always fills it). `args` and `env` keep their defaults and are
  ignored for an HTTP server.
- `connectMcpServer` (`src/mcp/client.ts`) takes `command?`, `url?` and `headers?`; a `url`
  builds `{ kind: "http", url, headers: headers ?? {} }`, otherwise today's stdio config.
- `createMcpPool` (`src/mcp/pool.ts`) passes `url` and `headers` through. An HTTP connection
  has `pid` null, so `onSpawn` never fires and the pid registry is untouched.
- `nax mcp lock`'s empty-server hint names the url for an HTTP server instead of
  `undefined`.
- Config descriptions (`src/cli/config-descriptions.ts`) gain `mcp.servers.<id>.url` and
  `mcp.servers.<id>.headers`, and `mcp.servers.<id>.command` says it is the stdio form.

**Scope** — In: descriptor/provider hint propagation, schema/runtime types, client/pool transport forwarding, HTTP lock hint and descriptions. Update the full parsed-server default expectation in test/unit/config/schemas-mcp.test.ts to include headers {}; every rejection case (empty command, unknown stage, bad id, unknown key) keeps its verdict. Out: catalog conversion (US-003–006), chat pool lifecycle (US-007), catalog lock enumeration (US-009). OAuth for remote MCP servers is not supported; an HTTP server gets only its static `headers`. SSE MCP transport is not supported anywhere; an `sse` catalog entry is listed as a diagnostic and dropped. MCP resources, prompts and sampling are not supported; only tools. Configured `mcp.servers` entries get no `${VAR}` expansion; an HTTP server configured there carries its headers literally, and the existing config secret scan still applies to them.

**Interface** — `McpToolDescriptor` gains `readonly readOnly?: true`; `McpServerConfig` gains `command?: string`, `url?: string`, `headers?: Record<string, string>`; `connectMcpServer(args)` accepts these optional transport fields with the existing serverId/workdir/args/env/connectTimeoutMs/signal/onSpawn fields. Preserve `createMcpProviders({ config, pool, projectRoot, storyId?, readLock?, onWithheld? }) -> readonly ToolProvider[]` of `kind: "discovered"`, including existing applyLock and allowedTools filtering. Prove the upstream seam by resolving a real createMcpProviders provider through resolveProviderTools and observing docs__put only in askTools.

**Security amendment (2026-10-25, user-approved after a security review)** — The read-only hint is server-stated and untrusted: a provider tool carries readOnly: true only when the live descriptor has readOnly: true AND the resolved lock lists the tool under readOnly[serverId]. McpLockFile gains optional readOnly: Record<serverId, toolName[]>; a malformed readOnly reads as none. Error text is redacted by its secret parts, not by matching the whole configured string (redactMcpReason(text, server) in src/mcp/pool.ts): the secrets are the url's username and password, every non-empty query value and the fragment (parsed with new URL), plus each non-empty headers value and each whitespace-separated token of it at least 4 characters long; each is replaced by *** in its raw, decodeURIComponent and encodeURIComponent forms. It applies to the connect-failed event reason, the warn log error field, and the error-as-data content call() returns to the model.

userStories.title: Discover Claude Code user and local MCP scopes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read Claude Code's .claude.json user/local MCP entries into the existing catalog and mark MCP delivery in /plugins wording.

**Motivation** — Most of the user's servers live in `~/.claude.json`.

**Approach** — Discovery portion of **3. Catalog MCP entries keep their connection spec (US-003 parsing, US-004 discovery).**

- `claudeJsonPath(env)` (`src/resources/claude-paths.ts`): `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json`
  when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, otherwise `<homedir>/.claude.json`. This is Claude Code's
  own location for the file.
- `discoverClaudeCodePackages({ repoRoot, claudeDir, claudeJson })`
  (`src/resources/claude-sources.ts`) reads `claudeJson` once. Its top-level `mcpServers`
  become the user package's `mcpServers` with scope `user`. Its
  `projects[repoRoot].mcpServers` (exact key match) come first in the project package's
  `mcpServers` with scope `local`, followed by the repo `.mcp.json` entries with scope
  `project`. A plugin's `.mcp.json` entries have scope `plugin`. Entries read from
  `claudeJson` carry `path` equal to the `claudeJson` path; user-scope entries have origin
  `claude-user` and local-scope entries origin `claude-project`. A missing file adds nothing
  and no diagnostic; a file that does not parse as a JSON object adds one `error` diagnostic
  to the user package; a `projects` or `mcpServers` value that is not an object adds one
  `error` diagnostic and nothing from that value.
- `loadResourceCatalog` passes `claudeJson: claudeJsonPath(env)`.
- `src/resources/index.ts` exports `parseMcpServers`, `claudeJsonPath` and the types
  `McpServerSpec` and `McpServerScope` (US-003, US-004).
- `formatPluginsListing` prints `mcp N` without `(not delivered yet)`; agents keep it until
  F5b.

**Interface** — `claudeJsonPath(env)` and `discoverClaudeCodePackages({ repoRoot, claudeDir, claudeJson })` extend the existing resources API; reuse upstream `parseMcpServers(path, servers, origin, scope)` rather than reparsing per entry. loadResourceCatalog keeps its `{ repoRoot, config, env, naxPluginPackages }` options contract.

**Scope** — In: path resolution, one file read, scope routing, diagnostics, loader forwarding and listing wording. Existing claude-sources.test.ts discover helper passes a missing fixture claudeJson path so every old expectation stays true. In listing.test.ts change only "mcp 1 (not delivered yet)" to "mcp 1" for sp@m; agents and hooks wording is unchanged. Out: typed parser implementation (US-003), merge precedence/expansion (US-005/006), connections (US-007) and run/lock opt-in (US-009). Per-project enable or disable lists that Claude Code keeps in `~/.claude.json` (for example `disabledMcpServers`, `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers` under `projects[<repo>]`) are not read; only `mcpServers` is. Claude Code's per-server approval settings for project `.mcp.json` servers (`enableAllProjectMcpServers`, `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers` in `settings.json` / `settings.local.json`) are not read; the nax trust gate plus the MCP lock replace them.

userStories.title: Normalize MCP server IDs and expand catalog variables
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide pure provider-safe ID normalization and shell-style catalog value expansion helpers.

**Motivation** — One MCP client, not two.

**Approach** — ID and expansion algorithms from **4. The merge (US-005 ids and expansion, US-006 merge).** New `packages/nax/src/resources/mcp-expand.ts` holds these helpers; export mcpServerId and expandMcpValue from src/resources/index.ts.

- Id: the base is the entry `name`, or `<plugin>-<name>` for an entry whose origin is
  `claude-plugin`. `mcpServerId(base)` lowercases it, replaces every run of characters
  outside `[a-z0-9_-]` with `-`, replaces every run of two or more `_` with one `_`, and
  strips leading characters that are not `[a-z0-9]`. An empty result drops the entry with
  an `error` diagnostic `[resources] mcp server name <name> in <path> yields no usable id`.
  Every nonempty result satisfies `MCP_SERVER_ID_RE` and contains no `__`; the helper returns an empty string when no usable id remains, as required by the !!! acceptance criterion.
- Expansion (`expandMcpValue(value: string, vars: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>):
  { readonly value: string } | { readonly missing: string }` in
  `src/resources/mcp-expand.ts`; `missing` names the first unset variable): every
  `${NAME}` becomes `vars[NAME]` (an empty string is a value); every `${NAME:-default}`
  becomes `vars[NAME]` when it is set and non-empty, otherwise `default` (shell `:-`
  semantics; the default runs to the first `}` and may be empty, nesting is not supported,
  and an unterminated `${` is copied literally). `NAME` matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; any other text,
  including a `$` not followed by `{`, is copied literally. `vars` is `input.env` plus, for a
  `claude-plugin` entry, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to that package's `root` (overriding the
  environment). It applies to `command`, each of `args`, each `env` value, `url` and each
  `headers` value; keys are never expanded. A `${NAME}` with no value and no default drops
  the entry with an `error` diagnostic
  `[resources] mcp server <id>: ${NAME} is not set`.

**Interface**
```ts
export function expandMcpValue(
  value: string,
  vars: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>,
): { readonly value: string } | { readonly missing: string };
export function mcpServerId(base: string): string;
```

**Scope** — In: pure helpers in mcp-expand.ts, deterministic return values and resources barrel exports. Out: plugin prefix/root selection, iteration over connection fields, diagnostic creation and dropping entries belong to the merge consumer (US-006); schema transport support belongs to US-002. Only nonempty IDs must match MCP_SERVER_ID_RE; the explicit empty-result sentinel for !!! is authoritative and the merge drops it. Configured `mcp.servers` entries get no `${VAR}` expansion; an HTTP server configured there carries its headers literally, and the existing config secret scan still applies to them.

userStories.title: Merge catalog MCP resources into connectable configuration
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert ordered catalog MCP resources into ordinary McpConfig entries with deterministic IDs, expansion, precedence and diagnostics.

**Motivation** — One MCP client, not two.

**Approach** — **4. The merge (US-005 ids and expansion, US-006 merge).** New `packages/nax/src/resources/mcp-merge.ts`:

**Interface**
```ts
export type McpServerSource = "config" | McpServerScope;

export interface MergedMcpServers {
  readonly config: McpConfig;
  /** Server id -> where the entry came from; plugin entries also carry the plugin name. */
  readonly sources: ReadonlyMap<string, { readonly source: McpServerSource; readonly plugin?: string }>;
  readonly diagnostics: readonly ResourceDiagnostic[];
}

export function mergeCatalogMcpServers(input: {
  readonly mcp: McpConfig | undefined;
  readonly catalog: ResourceCatalog;
  readonly env: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>;
}): MergedMcpServers;
```

- Order: every `input.mcp.servers` entry first (source `config`, copied unchanged), then the
  catalog's packages in package order (project, user, plugins) and each package's
  `mcpServers` in order. The first entry to claim an id wins. A later catalog entry with
  the same id is dropped with a `warn` diagnostic
  `[resources] mcp server <id> from <path> is shadowed by <winner>`, where `<winner>` is
  `config`, `local`, `project`, `user` or `plugin <name>`.
- Configured `mcp.servers` entries are not expanded; only catalog entries are.
- Id: the base is the entry `name`, or `<plugin>-<name>` for an entry whose origin is
  `claude-plugin`. `mcpServerId(base)` lowercases it, replaces every run of characters
  outside `[a-z0-9_-]` with `-`, replaces every run of two or more `_` with one `_`, and
  strips leading characters that are not `[a-z0-9]`. An empty result drops the entry with
  an `error` diagnostic `[resources] mcp server name <name> in <path> yields no usable id`.
  Every kept entry's nonempty id satisfies `MCP_SERVER_ID_RE` and contains no `__`; empty normalization is the explicit drop case, not a regex-matching result.
- Expansion (`expandMcpValue(value: string, vars: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>):
  { readonly value: string } | { readonly missing: string }` in
  `src/resources/mcp-expand.ts`; `missing` names the first unset variable): every
  `${NAME}` becomes `vars[NAME]` (an empty string is a value); every `${NAME:-default}`
  becomes `vars[NAME]` when it is set and non-empty, otherwise `default` (shell `:-`
  semantics; the default runs to the first `}` and may be empty, nesting is not supported,
  and an unterminated `${` is copied literally). `NAME` matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; any other text,
  including a `$` not followed by `{`, is copied literally. `vars` is `input.env` plus, for a
  `claude-plugin` entry, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to that package's `root` (overriding the
  environment). It applies to `command`, each of `args`, each `env` value, `url` and each
  `headers` value; keys are never expanded. A `${NAME}` with no value and no default drops
  the entry with an `error` diagnostic
  `[resources] mcp server <id>: ${NAME} is not set`.
- An `sse` entry is dropped with a `warn` diagnostic
  `[resources] mcp server <id>: transport sse is not supported`.
- A kept catalog entry becomes `McpServerConfig` with `stages: ["*"]`,
  `timeoutMs: MCP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `enabled: true`, `headers: {}` for stdio, and
  `args: []`, `env: {}` for http.
- `MCP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `MCP_SERVER_ID_RE` are added to the `@/config` barrel
  (`src/config/index.ts`) so `src/resources` imports them without an internal path
  (`check:alias-internals`). `mcpServerId` and `expandMcpValue` (US-005) and
  `mergeCatalogMcpServers` with its types (US-006) are exported from `src/resources/index.ts`.

**Scope** — In: pure merge, source map, origin-bearing diagnostics, value-field traversal and config/resources exports. Consume upstream mcp-expand.ts rather than reimplementing it. Nonempty IDs satisfy the regex; empty normalization is the documented drop sentinel. Build catalogs through buildResourceCatalog for parser/discovery seam assertions and prove HTTP output schema compatibility. Out: helper algorithms (US-005), discovery (US-003/004), chat reserved ID/enable filtering (US-007), async resolveCatalogMcpConfig and logging/run/lock integration (US-009). Configured `mcp.servers` entries get no `${VAR}` expansion; an HTTP server configured there carries its headers literally, and the existing config secret scan still applies to them. SSE MCP transport is not supported anywhere; an `sse` catalog entry is listed as a diagnostic and dropped.

userStories.title: Show live MCP provenance, connection status and withheld tools in /mcp
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete chat MCP observability and expose it through a built-in /mcp command.

**Motivation** — The catalog parses MCP entries and drops the useful half.

**Approach** — State/listing portion of **5. Chat wiring (US-007) and `/mcp` (US-008).** Extend upstream `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mcp.ts`.

- `createChatMcp` merges (Approach 4), keeps every enabled server, and sets each server's
  `stages` to `["*"]`: `stages` decides which `nax run` stages a server attaches to, and a
  chat session is not a pipeline stage. It builds the pool with
  `createMcpPool({ servers, retry: CHAT_MCP_RETRY })` and the providers with
  `createMcpProviders({ config: { servers }, pool, projectRoot: repoRoot, onWithheld })`,
  where `onWithheld` records the entry keyed by `serverId` plus `name`, replacing an earlier
  entry with the same key: `createMcpProviders` reports withheld tools on every `tools()`
  call and the chat resolves providers again on every session reopen (mode switch, model
  switch, `/clear`, resume), so `withheld()` returns each withheld tool once. `close()`
  closes the pool. With no enabled server it builds no pool and returns no providers.
- `state.servers` has one row per attached server: `id`, `source` and `plugin` from the
  merge's `sources`, and `transport` `http` when the server has a `url`, otherwise `stdio`.
  `state.events()` returns the pool's `events()` (an empty list when no pool was built).
- `state.diagnostics` is the merge diagnostics followed by the catalog diagnostics whose
  `path` ends in `.mcp.json` or `.claude.json`; `/skills` and `/plugins` do not show
  them for the project and user packages, so `/mcp` is where they are seen (a Claude Code
  plugin's `.mcp.json` diagnostic shows in both `/plugins` and `/mcp`).
- `src/chat/index.ts` exports `createChatMcp`, `formatMcpListing`, `CHAT_MCP_RETRY`,
  `_chatMcpDeps` and the types `ChatMcp`, `ChatMcpState` and `ChatMcpServerRow`.
- `/mcp` is a built-in slash command (after `/plugins` in the help list) that shows
  `formatMcpListing(host.mcp)`. One line per server:
  `<id>  <source label>  <transport>  <status>`, where the source label is `config`,
  `local`, `project`, `user` or `plugin <name>`; status is `connected, <n> tools` after the
  server's last `connected` event, `failed: <reason>` after a `connect-failed` event, and
  `not connected` before any event. When the lock withheld any of that server's tools the
  line ends `, <k> withheld (run nax mcp lock)`. Diagnostics follow, one per line, as
  `<severity>  <path>  <message>`. With no state or no servers it prints
  `(no MCP servers)`.
- Connection is lazy, as in `nax run`: the pool connects a server the first time the
  session resolves its tools, at session open. A mode switch reopens the session on the same
  pool, whose memoised entries (including a failed one) are reused.

**Interface**
```ts
export interface ChatMcpServerRow {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly source: McpServerSource;
  readonly plugin?: string;
  readonly transport: "stdio" | "http";
}

export interface ChatMcpState {
  readonly servers: readonly ChatMcpServerRow[];
  readonly diagnostics: readonly ResourceDiagnostic[];
  /** Pool connection events, read live for /mcp. */
  events(): readonly McpServerEvent[];
  /** Tools the lock withheld so far, read live for /mcp. */
  withheld(): readonly McpWithheldEntry[];
}

export function formatMcpListing(state: ChatMcpState | undefined): string;
```

**Scope** — In: finish/verify upstream state rows, live event reads, deduplicated withholding, diagnostic selection/order, exact listing text and built-in dispatch/help. formatMcpListing returns its rendered string without printing; runSlashCommand receives a parsed SlashCommand object and passes that string to show. ChatMcpState.withheld() returns an array, not an individual entry. Preserve upstream pool/lifecycle wiring while filling state; do not create a second pool. The test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx COMMANDS list gains mcp between plugins and quit so AC-16 help and AC-19 turn blocking include it. Assert runSlashCommand invokes show using host.mcp, including absent state. Out: provider/session wiring and teardown (US-007), approval enforcement (US-001), lock refresh and run configuration (US-009). A per-server enable or disable toggle inside chat is not added; `mcp.servers.<id>.enabled` and removing the catalog entry are the switches. F5b `chat-subagents` delivers subagents, the `Agent` tool, `/agents` and `agent.modelAliases`; this feature leaves `/plugins` printing `agents N (not delivered yet)`.

**Security amendment (2026-10-25)** — ChatMcpServerRow gains locked: boolean (false for a catalog server the lock does not list); formatMcpListing prints not locked (run nax mcp lock) as that row's status.
